description: Check whether you are on track for each exam. For every exam it gives the days left, the study days left, the hours still to study, the hours to put in on each study day and a plain On track or Behind verdict, using the same hours per day, hours per weekday and days off as the plan tools. Give from_date to count from a fixed day. Dates can be plain text, like Dec 12 or in 3 weeks. Example prompt: "Am I on track for my exam on 2026-12-12 if I can study 2 hours a day?"

exams.description: Exams with name, date, optional hours needed and optional topics with their own hours.

date.description: Date of the exam. Use 2026-12-12, or plain text like Dec 12, next Friday or in 3 weeks.

hours_needed.description: Study hours you want to put in. Defaults to 10.

topics.description: Topics of the exam with their own hours, so the plan can say which topic to study on each day.

hours_needed.description: Study hours for this topic. Leave it out to split the exam hours evenly over the topics.

name.description: Name of the topic inside the exam.

from_date.description: The day to count from. Defaults to today. Use 2026-12-12, or plain text like Dec 12, next Friday or in 3 weeks.

hours_per_day.description: Study hours available on a study day.

hours_per_weekday.description: Study hours for each weekday, like [{day: "mon", hours: 2}, {day: "sat", hours: 6}]. Weekdays you leave out use hours_per_day, a weekday with 0 hours is a day off, and days in days_off are always left out.

day.description: Weekday name, like mon, tue, sat or sunday.

hours.description: Study hours on that weekday. Use 0 for a day with no studying.

name: exam_countdown
title: Exam countdown
